Regulatory Notice

This work has been prepared for educational and professional reference purposes. It is designed for use by CIIN examination candidates, licensed insurance practitioners, and insurance industry professionals in Nigeria. It is not intended as legal, actuarial, financial, or regulatory advice. Readers requiring advice on specific regulatory, legal, or financial matters should consult appropriately qualified professionals.

The regulatory content in this work reflects the Nigerian insurance regulatory landscape as at the date of publication. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025 (NIIRA 2025), the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA 2023), the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 (GAID 2025), and all other legislation and regulatory instruments referenced are as at their versions current at the date of publication. Subsequent amendments, new circulars, and regulatory developments may affect the accuracy of specific provisions described.
CIIN Disclaimer

This work is not an official publication of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (CIIN). It is an independent professional reference aligned to the CIIN examination syllabus. The CIIN does not endorse, approve, or accept responsibility for the content of this work. Candidates preparing for CIIN examinations should refer to official CIIN study texts and examination guidance.
Data and Statistics Notice

Market data, premium income statistics, policy counts, and penetration figures cited in this work are sourced from publicly available publications (NAICOM Annual Reports, NIA statistics, EFInA surveys, NBS data) as at the date of research. These figures are subject to revision and readers should consult primary sources for current data.
Specimen Documents

The specimen documents in Appendix Set Two are for educational purposes only and are not legally binding instruments. Company names, policy numbers, and personal details are fictitious. These documents must not be used as actual insurance contracts, proposal forms, or quotations without adaptation by qualified legal and actuarial professionals.
First Edition
For every Nigerian insurance professional who
has fought to settle a valid claim on time,
explained insurance to a sceptical client,
or stayed in this industry long enough to believe
it can be what it should be.

Life Insurance in Nigeria: A Professional Body of Knowledge is the most comprehensive reference work on Nigerian life insurance practice ever compiled. It was developed by MTDL Limited to meet a specific and longstanding gap in the Nigerian insurance professional’s library: a single, authoritative, up-to-date reference that integrates the theory of insurance, the practice of Nigerian life insurance operations, the full requirements of the post-NIIRA 2025 regulatory framework, and the practical professional knowledge expected of candidates at every level of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria’s qualification pathway.

This work is not a study guide in the conventional sense. It does not summarise content for the purpose of passing examinations. It is a professional body of knowledge in the truest sense: the accumulated, structured knowledge that a well-rounded Nigerian life insurance professional should possess — from the foundations of insurance law and the principles of underwriting, through the full range of life insurance products, the complete operational and governance framework of a licensed Nigerian life insurer, and the technology, data, and emerging risk dimensions that will define the industry’s next decade.

The work is structured across eight parts and thirty-nine chapters. Its regulatory content is anchored in the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025 (NIIRA 2025), the most comprehensive reform of the Nigerian insurance regulatory framework in more than two decades. All chapters have been updated to reflect NIIRA 2025 in full, including its capital adequacy requirements, consumer protection obligations, Insurtech licensing framework, and Takaful provisions. The data privacy chapters are aligned to the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA 2023) and the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 (GAID 2025). The pension interface chapters are aligned to the Pension Reform Act 2014 and PenCom’s RLA market guidelines.

Three appendix sets provide reference tools designed for daily professional use: technical reference tables (including an illustrative EFU mortality table extract, NIIRA 2025 capital thresholds, and the CIIN qualification framework); specimen insurance documents annotated for educational purposes; and a comprehensive regulatory instruments log covering NAICOM circulars from 2020 to 2025, the NIIRA 2025 commencement tracker, the recapitalisation compliance timeline, the NDPC enforcement log, and the PenCom-NAICOM interface instruments.
CIIN Examination Candidates

This work covers the syllabus content of the CIIN’s Foundation (Certificate in Insurance), Diploma, and Associateship examinations for the life insurance pathway. Each chapter opens with learning objectives mapped to the examination competency level, and closes with practice questions graded at Foundation, Diploma, and Associateship level. Candidates are advised to use the official CIIN study texts as their primary study material and to use this work as the authoritative companion reference that provides the depth of context, the Nigerian market examples, and the regulatory detail that examination study texts cannot always provide.
Licensed Insurance Practitioners

For practitioners already working in Nigerian insurance, this work serves as the desk reference for operational, regulatory, and strategic matters. The regulatory chapters (particularly Chapters 4, 21, 24, 28–33) provide the most comprehensive available treatment of the post-NIIRA 2025 regulatory environment for Nigerian life insurers. The technology chapters (29–32) provide the framework for assessing and improving the insurer’s technology capability. The appendix sets provide working tools — the regulatory instruments log, specimen documents, and technical tables — for immediate professional use.
Insurance Managers and Executives

Senior practitioners will find the strategic chapters (Parts 5 and 7 in particular) directly applicable to the challenges of managing and growing a Nigerian life insurance company in the post-NIIRA 2025 environment. Chapter 27 (Strategy and Research), Chapter 34 (Structuring the Organisation), Chapter 35 (Human Capital and Culture), Chapter 36 (Accessing Industry Intelligence), and Chapter 33 (Emerging Risks and Industry Outlook) together provide a strategic management framework for the contemporary Nigerian life insurer.
Compliance and Risk Professionals

The regulatory, governance, and risk management chapters are written with the compliance and risk professional’s needs explicitly in mind. Chapter 21 (Market Conduct), Chapter 24 (Corporate Governance and Solvency), Chapter 15 (Enterprise Risk Management), Chapters 28–32 (Technology and Innovation), and Appendix Set Three (Regulatory Instruments Log) together constitute a comprehensive compliance reference for the NIIRA 2025 environment.
Trainers and Educators

The structure of each chapter — learning objectives, substantive content, boxed case studies and advisories, a glossary, and examination practice questions — makes this work directly usable as the curriculum backbone for insurance professional development programmes, in-house training, and executive education in the Nigerian insurance sector.
Chapter Structure

Learning Objectives: Each chapter opens with 8–12 learning objectives stating precisely what the reader should understand and be able to do on completing the chapter. The objectives are graded to indicate their relevant examination level.

Main Text: The substantive content of each chapter, organised into numbered sections and sub-sections. Key definitions are presented in definition boxes. Case studies, worked examples, and advisory frameworks are presented in distinctively coloured boxes.
Definition Boxes: Every significant technical term is defined in a bordered box at the point of first substantive use, enabling the work to function as both a narrative text and a reference.

Advisory and Case Boxes: Practical advisories, case studies, worked examples, and key warnings are presented in colour-coded boxes distinguished by their type: blue (information), green (process), amber (advisory), purple (case study), red (warning), and orange (key principle).
Glossary: Each chapter closes with a glossary of key terms introduced in that chapter. The comprehensive Glossary in Chapter 37 cross-references all terms across the full work.

CIIN Practice Questions: Ten examination-style practice questions at the close of each chapter, graded: Foundation (Cert. CIIN), Diploma (Dip. CIIN), and Associateship (ACIIN). Structured questions and essay questions are included at the higher levels.

References and Further Reading: An annotated bibliography at the close of each chapter, distinguishing between Nigerian regulatory sources, academic literature, and international industry publications.
Part One: Foundations of Insurance (Chapters 1–4)

Establishes the conceptual, legal, and regulatory foundation. Chapter 1 covers the nature and purpose of insurance; Chapter 2 the fundamental principles (insurable interest, utmost good faith, indemnity, contribution, subrogation); Chapter 3 insurance contract law; and Chapter 4 the Nigerian insurance regulatory framework from the Insurance Act 2003 through to NIIRA 2025.
Part Two: Life Insurance Products (Chapters 5–10)

Comprehensive survey of life assurance concepts and the full product range. Chapter 5 introduces life assurance concepts and terminology; Chapter 6 covers the complete product spectrum (term, whole life, endowment, unit-linked); Chapter 7 group life insurance; Chapter 8 annuities and retirement income products; Chapter 9 Takaful and Islamic insurance in Nigeria; and Chapter 10 life insurance product development and pricing.
Part Three: Technical Life Insurance Practice (Chapters 11–15)

The technical core of life insurance operations. Chapters 11–12 cover underwriting and claims management. Chapter 13 provides actuarial concepts for non-actuarial practitioners. Chapter 14 addresses reinsurance, including the NIIRA 2025 domestic cession requirement. Chapter 15 covers enterprise risk management for life insurance companies.
Part Four: Distribution, Marketing, and Customer Management (Chapters 16–22)

The complete distribution and customer management framework. Chapters 16–18 cover the full intermediary landscape (channels, agencies, brokers). Chapters 19–21 address marketing, customer service, and market conduct. Chapter 22 covers microinsurance and financial inclusion.
Part Five: Finance, Governance, and Strategy (Chapters 23–27)

The financial and strategic management of a life insurance company. Chapter 23 covers insurance fund investment and ALM; Chapter 24 corporate governance, solvency, and IFRS 17; Chapter 25 personal financial planning; Chapter 26 revenue architecture; and Chapter 27 strategy and competitive intelligence.
Part Six: Technology and Innovation (Chapters 28–33)

The technology and forward-looking dimension. Chapter 28 covers Insurtech and digital transformation; Chapter 29 Policy Administration Systems; Chapter 30 sales, operations, and customer service technology; Chapter 31 artificial intelligence use cases; Chapter 32 data privacy under NDPA 2023; and Chapter 33 emerging risks, compulsory insurance, and the industry outlook.
Part Seven: Organisation and Human Capital (Chapters 34–36)

The management of the insurance enterprise. Chapter 34 addresses organisational structure; Chapter 35 human capital, culture, and professional development; and Chapter 36 accessing industry research, data, and competitive intelligence.
Part Eight: Reference and Examination Preparation (Chapters 37–39)

The reference and examination resource. Chapter 37 is a comprehensive glossary of over 600 insurance and life assurance terms. Chapter 38 is the CIIN Examination Preparation Guide with examination strategies, syllabus mapping, and worked question guidance. Chapter 39 is the Regulatory Reference Index and annotated bibliography.
Appendix Set One: Technical Reference Tables

Five technical tables: an illustrative EFU Nigerian life mortality table extract (ages 20–70); NIIRA 2025 capital thresholds for all 14 licence classes; Insurtech licensing quick-reference (Partnering vs Standalone); NAICOM approved investment classes and portfolio limits; and the CIIN qualification framework overview including CPD categories.
Appendix Set Two: Specimen Documents

Five annotated specimen insurance documents: an individual term life assurance policy; a life assurance proposal form with guidance notes; a group life master policy (selected clauses); a Retirement Life Annuity quotation template with break-even analysis; and a life insurance death claims notification form with document checklist.
Appendix Set Three: Regulatory Instruments Log

A structured regulatory reference log: Log 3A (NAICOM circulars 2020–2025); Log 3B (NIIRA 2025 commencement tracker); Log 3C (recapitalisation compliance timeline); Log 3D (NDPC insurance sector enforcement log); and Log 3E (PenCom-NAICOM interface instruments including the RLA regulatory workflow).

blocks.text: Principal Regulatory Instruments Referenced in This Work

blocks.h: Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025 (NIIRA 2025)

Act No. 2 of 2025. Signed 6 August 2025. The primary legislative framework for insurance in Nigeria, replacing the Insurance Act 2003. Covers licensing, capital adequacy, risk-based capital, product approval, consumer protection, Insurtech licensing, Takaful, reinsurance, corporate governance, investment, AML/CFT, data protection, enforcement, and transitional provisions. Referred to throughout this work as NIIRA 2025.
NAICOM Insurtech Guidelines 2025

Subsidiary regulation issued by NAICOM (National Insurance Commission) under NIIRA 2025, effective August 2025. Covers Partnering and Standalone Insurtech licensing, the regulatory sandbox, AI/ML model governance, cybersecurity standards, and embedded insurance provisions. Referred to as the Insurtech Guidelines.
Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA 2023)

Signed 12 June 2023. The primary data protection legislation in Nigeria, establishing the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and creating comprehensive data subject rights and controller obligations. Applicable to all licensed insurers as Data Controllers/Processors of Major Importance.
General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 (GAID 2025)

The NDPC’s primary implementation directive under NDPA 2023, effective 19 September 2025. Specifies data localisation, retention periods, DPIA requirements, and compliance programme obligations. Referred to as GAID 2025.
Pension Reform Act 2014 (PRA 2014)

Cap P4, LFN. The primary legislation governing the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), mandatory group life insurance, and the Retirement Life Annuity (RLA) product market. Administered by PenCom. Cross-referenced in Chapters 7, 8, 30, 31, 33.
National Health Insurance Authority Act 2022 (NHIA Act)

Signed 19 May 2022. Replaces the NHIS Act 1999. Establishes the National Health Insurance Authority and the framework for universal health coverage and Health Maintenance Organisation (HMO) regulation.
NAICOM Act 1997 (Cap N53, LFN)
Establishes the National Insurance Commission as Nigeria’s apex insurance regulator. Continues in force alongside NIIRA 2025.
CIIN Act 1993 (Cap C10, LFN)

Establishes the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (CIIN) as the professional body for insurance. NIIRA 2025 cross-references CIIN qualifications as the minimum professional standard for regulated insurance roles.
Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 (MLPPA 2022)
The primary AML/CFT legislation applicable to insurers. Cross-referenced in Chapter 21.
Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 (CAMA 2020)
The primary Nigerian corporate law applicable to all licensed insurers. Cross-referenced in Chapters 24 and 34.
